speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
text: asked the Minister for National Development whether the CPF Board will consider aligning the life expectancy factor with the Department of Statistics Singapore's reported average of 83.5 years when tabulating how much CPF savings can be used to purchase a property, instead of the existing 95 years.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And I acknowledge that there are many seniors who are living beyond 83.5 years.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: At the same time, there are also many others who do not live till 83.5.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And in my interactions with several of my residents, I have met a couple of categories who are unable to get onto the home ownership journey but who have extenuating circumstances that I think may merit a deeper look into this requirement.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The two groups of residents are: one, they are renting on the open market, typically mid-career, hit by some midlife crisis, perhaps career, perhaps marriage.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Their incomes are too high to rent Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats, but at the same time they cannot own in the private sector.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, therefore rising rental cost in the private market is a big concern for them.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I seek HDB's consideration to review whether we can do something for these categories.
